To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a method to identify and quantify selected biomarkers in histological sections using in-source decay imaging and MALDI FTICR mass analysis.
we developed a method for rapid identification of selected biomarkers in histological sections with minimal sample treatment.

the proposed method is a proof of concept that allows one to identify simultaneously, with minimal sample treatment and in a single experiment, a set of selected protein biomarkers on histopathological slices using in-source decay imaging MALDI-FT-ICR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for rapid detection of a set of selected proteins in histological sections.
the development of an in-source decay (radical induced fragmentation) imaging technique for protein analysis in tissue.
the development of new methods for the analysis of proteins and peptides by MALDI-FT-ICR MS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of in-source decay imaging and MALDI-FT ICR mass spectrometry provides a new approach to protein identification and differential analysis on tissue slices.

this work presents a proof of concept of an original method that allows one to identify simultaneously selected biomarkers in histological slices with a high dynamic range, using in-source decay MALDI MSI and MALDI FTICR.
this work presents the first demonstration of a targeted biomarker detection by in-source decay imaging using MALDI FTICR MS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for the direct identification of proteins on histology slices with minimal sample preparation using MALDI-FTMS.

we present a proof-of-concept for a method that enables the identification of a selected set of biomarkers in histological sections with minimal sample treatment, using in-source decay mass spectrometry and MALDI-FT-ICR.
we have demonstrated that MALDI-FT-ICR MSI can be used for rapid targeted biomarkers detection in histological slices with a minimal sample treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of 1,5-DAM as a MALDI matrix allows one to obtain a large tag for protein identification by MALDI-FTMS in-source decay imaging.
the use of 1,5-DAM matrix and the combination of MALDI-MSI with FTICR-MSI allow for the identification of a set of biomarkers with a minimal sample preparation.
MALDI-FTIR imaging is a very promising tool for targeted biomarker detection on histological sections with a very high spatial resolution.
